title: Tuples
paragraphs: A tuple is a data structure that stores multiple values in a specific order, similar to a list.
Unlike a list, a tuple is immutable, meaning its values cannot be added, removed, or changed after the tuple is created.
A tuple is created by separating values with commas (,), usually inside parentheses (()).
Tuples are useful for storing collections of values that should remain unchanged.

title: Similarities Between Tuples and Lists
paragraphs: Tuples and lists are both ordered collections, meaning their values are stored in a specific order.
Like lists, tuple values can be accessed using positive or negative indices and sections can be accessed using slicing.
You can traverse a tuple with a for loop, check membership using in, and find its length using len().
The main difference is that a tuple cannot be modified after it is created.

title: Mutability vs Immutability
paragraphs: A mutable object can be changed after it is created, while an immutable object cannot.
Lists are mutable, so their items can be added, removed, or replaced.
Tuples are immutable, so their items cannot.
If a tuple contains a mutable object (like a list), the mutable object within the tuple can still be modified as normal.
